source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

verses.rationale: Retains Paul's commissioned role, divine agency and Timothy's family designation.
verses.before: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through God’s will, and Timothy our brother,
verses.after: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and Timothy our brother,
verses.tsw_comparator: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother,

verses.rationale: Keeps the location, paired community descriptions and the pinned source's short blessing.
verses.before: to the holy and faithful brothers and sisters in Christ at Colossae: Grace to you and peace from God our Father.
verses.after: to the saints and faithful brothers and sisters in Christ at Colossae: Grace and peace to you from God our Father.
verses.tsw_comparator: To the holy and faithful brothers and sisters in Christ in Colossae: Grace to you and peace from God our Father.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated thanksgiving and names its addressee and occasion.
verses.before: We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you,
verses.after: We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you,
verses.tsw_comparator: We always give thanks to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you,

verses.rationale: Keeps faith's object and love's comprehensive human direction.
verses.before: because we have heard of your trust in Christ Jesus and the love you have for all the holy ones,
verses.after: because we have heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and the love you have for all the saints,
verses.tsw_comparator: since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of the love that you have for all the holy ones,

verses.rationale: Preserves hope as the ground and retains both word-of-truth and good-news descriptions.
verses.before: because of the hope stored up for you in heaven. You heard about this hope before in the word of truth, the good news,
verses.after: because of the hope stored up for you in heaven. You heard about this hope beforehand in the word of truth, the good news
verses.tsw_comparator: because of the hope laid up for you in the heavens, which you heard beforehand in the word of truth, the good news,

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired growth images, worldwide scope and the local beginning.
verses.before: which has come to you. Just as it is bearing fruit and growing in the whole world, so it has been among you since the day you heard and truly knew God’s grace.
verses.after: that has come to you. Just as it is bearing fruit and growing throughout the whole world, so it has among you since the day you heard it and truly understood God's grace.
verses.tsw_comparator: which has come to you, just as in all the world it is bearing fruit and growing, as it also does among you from the day you heard it and understood the grace of God in truth,

verses.rationale: Retains Epaphras's name, slave language and representative service.
verses.before: You learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful servant of Christ on our behalf,
verses.after: You learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow slave, who is a faithful minister of Christ on our behalf.
verses.tsw_comparator: just as you learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ on our behalf,

verses.rationale: Keeps the report and its spiritual setting without expanding the relation.
verses.before: and who also made known to us your love in the Spirit.
verses.after: He also told us about your love in the Spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: and who has made known to us your love in the Spirit.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unceasing prayer, filling image and full pair of cognitive gifts.
verses.before: For this reason, from the day we heard, we have not stopped praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of God’s will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
verses.after: For this reason, from the day we heard, we have not stopped praying for you and asking that you be filled with the knowledge of his will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
verses.tsw_comparator: For this reason also, from the day we heard it, we have not ceased praying for you, asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,

verses.rationale: Keeps walk and fruit metaphors with the repeated growth language.
verses.before: so that you may walk worthy of the Lord, pleasing him in every way, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God,
verses.after: so that you may walk worthy of the Lord and please him in every way: bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God,
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may walk worthy of the Lord, fully pleasing to him, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God,

verses.rationale: Retains the piling up of power terms and the purpose of steadfast endurance.
verses.before: being strengthened with all power according to his glorious might for all endurance and patience, with joy,
verses.after: being strengthened with every kind of power according to his glorious might, for all endurance and patience, with joy
verses.tsw_comparator: being strengthened with all power, according to his glorious might, for all endurance and patience with joy,

verses.rationale: Preserves divine enablement, inheritance and light imagery.
verses.before: giving thanks to the Father who has made you fit to share in the inheritance of the holy ones in the light.
verses.after: giving thanks to the Father, who has enabled you to share in the inheritance of the saints in the light.
verses.tsw_comparator: giving thanks to the Father, who has qualified you to share in the inheritance of the holy ones in light.

verses.rationale: Keeps both movements, the authority language and the Son's relational description.
verses.before: He rescued us from the authority of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son,
verses.after: He rescued us from the authority of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son,
verses.tsw_comparator: He has rescued us from the authority of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of his love,

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned reading without adding blood and preserves the explanatory apposition.
verses.before: in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.
verses.after: in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.

verses.rationale: Retains both elevated titles without resolving their theological relation in the verse.
verses.before: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation,
verses.after: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation,
verses.tsw_comparator: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation;

verses.rationale: Keeps the cosmic pairs, four powers and threefold relation to creation.
verses.before: because in him all things were created in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible—whether thrones, dominions, rulers, or authorities. All things have been created through him and for him.
verses.after: because in him all things were created—in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones, dominions, rulers or authorities. All things were created through him and for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: for in him all things were created, in the heavens and on the earth, the visible and the invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities—all things have been created through him and for him.

verses.rationale: Preserves temporal precedence and sustaining cohesion.
verses.before: He is before all things, and in him all things hold together.
verses.after: He is before all things, and in him all things hold together.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he is before all things, and in him all things hold together.

verses.rationale: Keeps the body image and repeated primacy language.
verses.before: He is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that he might become first in everything,
verses.after: He is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that he might be supreme in everything.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he is the head of the body, the church; he is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that in everything he might be preeminent.

verses.rationale: Preserves the compressed personified wording without supplying an unstated subject.
verses.before: because all the fullness was pleased to dwell in him,
verses.after: For all the fullness was pleased to dwell in him
verses.tsw_comparator: For in him all the fullness was pleased to dwell,

verses.rationale: Retains universal reconciliation, violent means and the earth/heaven scope.
verses.before: and through him to reconcile all things to himself, making peace through the blood of his cross—through him, whether things on earth or things in heaven.
verses.after: and through him to reconcile all things to himself—making peace through the blood of his cross—whether things on earth or things in heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: and through him to reconcile all things to himself, whether things on earth or things in heaven, making peace through the blood of his cross.

verses.rationale: Keeps prior estrangement and hostility tied to conduct without softening the accusation.
verses.before: You once were alienated and hostile in your minds, shown by evil works.
verses.after: And you, who were once alienated and hostile in mind, as shown by evil deeds—
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, who once were alienated and hostile in mind, doing evil deeds,

verses.rationale: Retains fleshly embodiment, death and all three intended qualities.
verses.before: But now he has reconciled you in his fleshly body through death, to present you holy, blameless, and above accusation before him,
verses.after: he has now reconciled in his physical body through death, to present you holy, blameless and beyond accusation before him,
verses.tsw_comparator: he has now reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, in order to present you holy and blameless and beyond reproach before him—

verses.rationale: Preserves the condition, building stability and the letter's expansive proclamation claim.
verses.before: if indeed you continue in the trust, founded and firm, not moving away from the hope of the good news you heard, which has been proclaimed in all creation under heaven. I, Paul, became its servant.
verses.after: provided that you remain in the faith, firmly founded and steadfast, not shifting away from the hope of the good news you heard, which was proclaimed in all creation under heaven and of which I, Paul, became a minister.
verses.tsw_comparator: if indeed you continue in the faith, grounded and steadfast, and not shifting from the hope of the good news that you heard. This good news has been proclaimed in all creation under heaven, and I, Paul, became a servant of it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult lack-and-filling language and identifies the body without explaining it away.
verses.before: Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and in my flesh I fill up what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions for the sake of his body, which is the church.
verses.after: Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and in my flesh I fill up what is lacking in Christ's afflictions for the sake of his body, which is the church.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I rejoice in my sufferings for your sake, and I fill up what is lacking in the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for the sake of his body, which is the church,

verses.rationale: Preserves commissioned stewardship and the ambiguous fullness expression.
verses.before: I became its servant according to the stewardship God gave me for you, to make God’s word fully known,
verses.after: I became its minister according to the stewardship God gave me for you, to bring God's word to fullness—
verses.tsw_comparator: of which I became a servant according to the stewardship from God that was given to me for you, to make the word of God fully known,

verses.rationale: Keeps the long concealment and present disclosure.
verses.before: the mystery hidden for ages and generations but now revealed to his holy ones.
verses.after: the mystery hidden for ages and generations but now revealed to his saints.
verses.tsw_comparator: the mystery hidden for ages and generations but now revealed to his holy ones,

verses.rationale: Retains nations, communal indwelling and the appositional hope.
verses.before: God wanted to make known among the Gentiles the glorious riches of this mystery: Christ in you, the hope of glory.
verses.after: God wanted to make known to them the glorious riches of this mystery among the nations: Christ in you, the hope of glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: to whom God chose to make known what are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.

verses.rationale: Preserves the threefold every-person emphasis and both instructional actions.
verses.before: He is the one we proclaim, warning every person and teaching every person with all wisdom so that we may present every person mature in Christ.
verses.after: We proclaim him, warning every person and teaching every person with all wisdom, so that we may present every person mature in Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: Him we proclaim, warning everyone and teaching everyone with all wisdom, so that we may present everyone mature in Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps labor, contest and the repeated working/energy wording.
verses.before: For this I labor, struggling according to his power that works powerfully in me.
verses.after: For this I labor and struggle, according to his energy powerfully at work in me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this I labor, striving according to his working that works in me in power.

verses.rationale: Preserves the named city and bodily absence alongside the breadth of concern.
verses.before: I want you to know how great a struggle I have for you, for those in Laodicea, and for all who have not seen me face to face,
verses.after: I want you to know how great a struggle I have for you, for those in Laodicea and for all who have not seen my face in the flesh,
verses.tsw_comparator: For I want you to know how great a struggle I have for you and for those in Laodicea and for all who have not seen me face to face,

verses.rationale: Keeps encouragement, love's joining work and Christ as the mystery's apposition.
verses.before: so that their hearts may be encouraged, joined together in love, and brought into all the riches of full assurance that comes from understanding, to know God’s mystery, Christ,
verses.after: so that their hearts may be encouraged, joined together in love, and reach all the riches of full assurance in understanding: the knowledge of God's mystery, Christ,
verses.tsw_comparator: that their hearts may be encouraged, being knit together in love, and into all the riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the knowledge of the mystery of God, which is Christ,

verses.rationale: Retains treasure and concealment imagery with their comprehensive scope.
verses.before: in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.
verses.after: in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.
verses.tsw_comparator: in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.

verses.rationale: Keeps the warning's purpose and rhetoric's attractive power.
verses.before: I say this so that no one deceives you with persuasive speech.
verses.after: I say this so that no one may deceive you with persuasive speech.
verses.tsw_comparator: I say this so that no one may deceive you with persuasive speech.

verses.rationale: Preserves the flesh/spirit contrast and the two disciplined stability images.
verses.before: For although I am absent in body, I am with you in spirit, rejoicing to see your order and the firmness of your trust in Christ.
verses.after: For though I am absent in the flesh, I am with you in spirit, rejoicing to see your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: For even though I am absent in the flesh, yet I am with you in spirit, rejoicing to see your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps reception as the basis and the recurring walk metaphor.
verses.before: Therefore, just as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, walk in him,
verses.after: Therefore, just as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, continue to walk in him,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in him,

verses.rationale: Retains the mixed plant/building images and ongoing grammatical aspect.
verses.before: rooted and built up in him, established in the trust just as you were taught, overflowing with thanksgiving.
verses.after: rooted and being built up in him, established in the faith as you were taught, and overflowing with thanksgiving.
verses.tsw_comparator: being rooted and built up in him and established in the faith, just as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving.

verses.rationale: Keeps the captive image, human tradition and the difficult elemental-powers expression.
verses.before: Watch out that no one takes you captive through philosophy and empty deception, according to human tradition, according to the elemental powers of the world, and not according to Christ.
verses.after: Watch out that no one takes you captive through philosophy and empty deception, according to human tradition and the elemental powers of the world, and not according to Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: See to it that no one takes you captive through philosophy and empty deception, according to human tradition, according to the elemental principles of the world, and not according to Christ.

verses.rationale: Preserves fullness, deity and bodily dwelling together.
verses.before: For in him all the fullness of deity dwells bodily,
verses.after: For in him all the fullness of deity dwells bodily,
verses.tsw_comparator: For in him all the fullness of deity dwells bodily,

verses.rationale: Keeps the shared fullness and supremacy over named powers.
verses.before: and you have been filled in him, who is the head over every ruler and authority.
verses.after: and you have been filled in him, who is the head of every ruler and authority.
verses.tsw_comparator: and you have been filled in him, who is the head of every ruler and authority.

verses.rationale: Retains circumcision and bodily stripping images without substituting a doctrinal paraphrase.
verses.before: In him you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hands, in the removal of the body of flesh, in the circumcision of Christ,
verses.after: In him you were also circumcised with a circumcision not performed by hands, in the stripping off of the body of flesh, in Christ's circumcision.
verses.tsw_comparator: In him also you were circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, in the removal of the body of flesh, in the circumcision of Christ,

verses.rationale: Keeps co-burial, co-resurrection and divine agency.
verses.before: having been buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through trust in the powerful working of God, who raised him from the dead.
verses.after: You were buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in God's power, who raised him from the dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: having been buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead.

verses.rationale: Preserves death/life reversal and the shift from you to us.
verses.before: And when you were dead in trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made you alive together with him, forgiving us all our trespasses.
verses.after: Though you were dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made you alive together with him, forgiving us all our trespasses.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, who were dead in trespasses and in the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses,

verses.rationale: Keeps the documentary image, opposition and crucifixion action.
verses.before: He erased the record of debt with its decrees that stood against us. He removed it from the way, nailing it to the cross.
verses.after: He erased the written record against us, with its decrees that opposed us. He took it away, nailing it to the cross.
verses.tsw_comparator: having erased the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands. This he set aside, nailing it to the cross.

verses.rationale: Retains the stripping and triumphal-procession images while leaving the final pronoun open.
verses.before: He stripped the rulers and authorities and made a public example of them, triumphing over them in the cross.
verses.after: He stripped the rulers and authorities and exposed them publicly, triumphing over them in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He disarmed the rulers and authorities and made a public display of them, triumphing over them in it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the complete calendar and dietary list.
verses.before: Therefore do not let anyone judge you about food or drink, or with respect to a festival, new moon, or Sabbath.
verses.after: Therefore, do not let anyone judge you about food or drink, or regarding a festival, new moon or Sabbaths.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore let no one judge you in matters of food and drink or with regard to a festival or a new moon or Sabbaths—

verses.rationale: Keeps shadow/body contrast while making the bodily metaphor intelligible.
verses.before: These are a shadow of the things to come, but the substance belongs to Christ.
verses.after: These are a shadow of what was to come, but the substance belongs to Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: which are a shadow of the things to come, but the substance belongs to Christ.

verses.rationale: Retains the pinned seen reading, judicial image and ironic false humility.
verses.before: Do not let anyone disqualify you, delighting in self-abasement and worship of angels, dwelling on visions, puffed up without reason by a fleshly mind,
verses.after: Do not let anyone disqualify you by delighting in humility and worship of angels, going on about what he has seen, puffed up without cause by his fleshly mind.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let no one disqualify you, insisting on humility and worship of angels, going on about visions, puffed up without reason by a fleshly mind,

verses.rationale: Keeps anatomical cohesion and emphatic divine growth.
verses.before: and not holding fast to the head, from whom the whole body, supported and held together by joints and ligaments, grows with growth from God.
verses.after: Such a person does not hold fast to the head, from whom the whole body, supported and held together by joints and ligaments, grows with growth from God.
verses.tsw_comparator: and not holding fast to the head, from whom the whole body, nourished and knit together through its joints and ligaments, grows with a growth that is from God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the conditional death and rhetorical challenge.
verses.before: If you died with Christ to the elemental powers of the world, why, as though still living in the world, do you submit to regulations:
verses.after: If you died with Christ to the elemental powers of the world, why, as though still living in the world, do you submit to decrees:
verses.tsw_comparator: If with Christ you died to the elemental principles of the world, why, as though living in the world, do you submit to regulations—

verses.rationale: Keeps the terse escalating quoted prohibitions.
verses.before: “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch”?
verses.after: “Do not handle! Do not taste! Do not touch!”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch”?

verses.rationale: Retains perishability and human origin.
verses.before: These things are all destined to perish with use; they are based on human commands and teachings.
verses.after: All these things perish as they are used, since they are based on human commands and teachings.
verses.tsw_comparator: These refer to things that perish with use, according to human commands and teachings.

verses.rationale: Keeps apparent wisdom, bodily severity and the difficult negative assessment.
verses.before: Such practices have an appearance of wisdom in self-made religion, self-abasement, and severe treatment of the body, but they have no value in restraining fleshly indulgence.
verses.after: Such practices have a reputation for wisdom in self-made religion, humility and harsh treatment of the body, but they are of no value against indulgence of the flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: These have indeed an appearance of wisdom in self-made religion and humility and severe treatment of the body, but they are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh.

verses.rationale: Preserves co-resurrection, spatial imagery and enthronement.
verses.before: Therefore, if you were raised with Christ, seek the things above, where Christ is seated at God’s right hand.
verses.after: Therefore, if you were raised with Christ, seek what is above, where Christ is seated at God's right hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sharp directional contrast.
verses.before: Set your minds on the things above, not on things on the earth,
verses.after: Set your minds on what is above, not on earthly things,
verses.tsw_comparator: Set your mind on the things above, not on the things on the earth.

verses.rationale: Retains the paradox of death and concealed life.
verses.before: because you died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
verses.after: for you died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.

verses.rationale: Keeps Christ as life and the paired future disclosure.
verses.before: When Christ, who is your life, is revealed, then you also will be revealed with him in glory.
verses.after: When Christ, your life, is revealed, then you too will be revealed with him in glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Christ—who is your life—is revealed, then you also will be revealed with him in glory.

verses.rationale: Preserves violent mortification imagery and the full vice list.
verses.before: Therefore put to death what belongs to your earthly life: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and greed, which is idolatry.
verses.after: So put to death what belongs to your earthly nature: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire and greed, which is idolatry.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore put to death whatever in you is earthly: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and greed, which is idolatry.

verses.rationale: Retains the variant-marked clause in the pinned main text and its relational idiom.
verses.before: Because of these things God’s wrath is coming.
verses.after: Because of these things God's wrath is coming on the children of disobedience.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of these things the wrath of God is coming.

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired walk/live description of former conduct.
verses.before: You too once walked in these things when you lived in them.
verses.after: You too once walked in these ways when you lived among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: In these things you too once walked, when you were living in them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the clothing-removal image and complete speech-related list.
verses.before: But now you must put them all away: anger, rage, malice, slander, and abusive speech from your mouth.
verses.after: But now you too must put away all these things: anger, rage, malice, slander and obscene speech from your mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: But now you must put away all such things: anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy speech from your mouth.

verses.rationale: Retains mutual scope and the clothing metaphor.
verses.before: Do not lie to one another, since you have stripped off the old humanity with its practices
verses.after: Do not lie to one another, since you have stripped off the old self with its practices
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not lie to one another, since you have stripped off the old self with its practices

verses.rationale: Keeps ongoing renewal, knowledge and restored image.
verses.before: and have put on the new humanity, which is being renewed in knowledge according to the image of its Creator.
verses.after: and put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge according to the image of its Creator.
verses.tsw_comparator: and have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge according to the image of its Creator.

verses.rationale: Preserves every social pair, including slavery, and the climactic Christ claim.
verses.before: Here there is no Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, slave, free—but Christ is all and in all.
verses.after: Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave or free; instead, Christ is all and in all.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that renewal there is no Greek and Judean, circumcised and uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave and free; but Christ is all, and in all.

verses.rationale: Keeps identity as the basis and the bodily compassion/clothing images.
verses.before: Therefore, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with deep compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience,
verses.after: Therefore, as God's chosen, holy and beloved people, clothe yourselves with heartfelt compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, as God’s chosen ones—holy and beloved—clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.

verses.rationale: Preserves reciprocal endurance, real complaint and the stated pattern.
verses.before: bearing with one another and forgiving each other if anyone has a complaint against another. Just as the Lord forgave you, so you also must forgive.
verses.after: Bear with one another and forgive each other if anyone has a complaint against another. Just as the Lord forgave you, so you also must forgive.
verses.tsw_comparator: Bear with one another and forgive each other; if anyone has a complaint against another, just as the Lord forgave you, so you also must forgive.

verses.rationale: Keeps clothing and binding images while rendering completeness as maturity.
verses.before: Above all these put on love, which is the bond of maturity.
verses.after: Above all these, put on love, which is the bond of maturity.
verses.tsw_comparator: And over all these, put on love, which binds everything together in completeness.

verses.rationale: Retains the umpire-like ruling verb, communal body and terse command.
verses.before: Let Christ’s peace rule in your hearts, to which you were called in one body. And be thankful.
verses.after: Let Christ's peace rule in your hearts, since you were called to this peace in one body. And be thankful.
verses.tsw_comparator: And let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, to which indeed you were called in one body. And be thankful.

verses.rationale: Keeps mutual teaching, three song forms and interior gratitude.
verses.before: Let Christ’s word dwell richly among you, teaching and warning one another with all wisdom, singing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.
verses.after: Let Christ's word dwell richly among you. Teach and warn one another with all wisdom; with psalms, hymns and spiritual songs, sing to God with gratitude in your hearts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; teach and admonish one another in all wisdom; with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, sing to God with gratitude in your hearts.

verses.rationale: Preserves comprehensive scope and mediated thanksgiving.
verses.before: Whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
verses.after: Whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.

verses.rationale: Retains the gender-specific command and its explicit qualification.
verses.before: Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
verses.after: Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wives, be subject to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.

verses.rationale: Preserves the reciprocal gender-specific command and prohibition of bitterness.
verses.before: Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them.
verses.after: Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them.

verses.rationale: Keeps children, both parents and the comprehensive command.
verses.before: Children, obey your parents in everything, because this is pleasing in the Lord.
verses.after: Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing in the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing in the Lord.

verses.rationale: Retains male-specific address and the child's harmful outcome.
verses.before: Fathers, do not provoke your children so that they do not become discouraged.
verses.after: Fathers, do not provoke your children, so that they do not become discouraged.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fathers, do not provoke your children, lest they become discouraged.

verses.rationale: Names slavery and masters directly, retaining surveillance and divided allegiance.
verses.before: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not with eye-service as people-pleasers, but with sincerity of heart, fearing the Lord.
verses.after: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only when they are watching, as people-pleasers, but with sincere hearts, fearing the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything—not with eye-service, as people-pleasers, but with sincerity of heart, fearing the Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps inner-source language and the explicit contrast.
verses.before: Whatever you do, work from the heart, as for the Lord and not for people,
verses.after: Whatever you do, work from the heart, as for the Lord and not for people,
verses.tsw_comparator: Whatever you do, work from the heart, as for the Lord and not for people,

verses.rationale: Retains the inheritance paradox and slave verb directed to Christ.
verses.before: knowing that from the Lord you will receive the inheritance as your reward. You serve the Lord Christ.
verses.after: knowing that from the Lord you will receive the inheritance as your reward. You serve the Lord Christ as a slave.
verses.tsw_comparator: knowing that from the Lord you will receive the inheritance as your reward. You serve the Lord Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps accountability and impartiality without restricting the wrongdoer.
verses.before: For the one who does wrong will receive back the wrong they have done, and there is no partiality.
verses.after: For the one who does wrong will be repaid for that wrong, and there is no favoritism.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the wrongdoer will be repaid for the wrong they have done, and there is no partiality.

verses.rationale: Names both master-slave relations and subjects human masters to another Master.
verses.before: Masters, give your slaves what is right and fair, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.
verses.after: Masters, provide your slaves what is right and fair, knowing that you too have a Master in heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Masters, grant to your servants what is just and fair, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.

verses.rationale: Preserves persistence, watchfulness and gratitude.
verses.before: Devote yourselves to prayer, staying alert in it with thanksgiving.
verses.after: Devote yourselves to prayer, staying alert in it with thanksgiving.
verses.tsw_comparator: Continue steadfastly in prayer, being watchful in it with thanksgiving,

verses.rationale: Keeps the door metaphor, plural request and imprisonment.
verses.before: At the same time pray for us too, that God may open a door for the word so that we may speak Christ’s mystery, for which I am in chains,
verses.after: At the same time, pray for us too, that God may open a door for the word, so that we may speak Christ's mystery, for which I am in chains.
verses.tsw_comparator: at the same time praying also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, on account of which I am in chains,

verses.rationale: Preserves the obligation and clarity sought.
verses.before: so that I may make it clear, as I ought to speak.
verses.after: Pray that I may make it clear, as I ought to speak.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that I may make it clear, as I ought to speak.

verses.rationale: Keeps social location, walk metaphor and redeemed-opportunity idiom.
verses.before: Walk wisely toward outsiders, making the most of the opportunity.
verses.after: Walk wisely toward outsiders, making the most of the time.
verses.tsw_comparator: Walk in wisdom toward those outside, making the most of the time.

verses.rationale: Retains the salt image, every occasion and individual response.
verses.before: Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you should answer each person.
verses.after: Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer each person.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you ought to answer each person.

verses.rationale: Preserves the name and all three relational/service titles.
verses.before: Tychicus, our beloved brother, faithful servant, and fellow slave in the Lord, will tell you everything about me.
verses.after: Tychicus, our beloved brother, faithful minister and fellow slave in the Lord, will tell you everything about me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Tychicus will make known to you all my affairs; he is a beloved brother and faithful minister and fellow servant in the Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps the messenger's two purposes and communal encouragement.
verses.before: I am sending him to you for this very reason, so that you may know about us and he may encourage your hearts,
verses.after: I am sending him to you for this very reason: that you may know how we are and that he may encourage your hearts.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that you may know our circumstances and that he may encourage your hearts,

verses.rationale: Names Onesimus and his local belonging without concealing his later slave context.
verses.before: together with Onesimus, our faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will tell you everything happening here.
verses.after: He is coming with Onesimus, our faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will tell you everything happening here.
verses.tsw_comparator: together with Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you everything that has taken place here.

verses.rationale: Retains all names, kinship and conditional reception instruction.
verses.before: Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, as does Mark, Barnabas’ cousin. You received instructions about him: if he comes to you, welcome him.
verses.after: Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, as does Mark, Barnabas's cousin. You received instructions about him: if he comes to you, welcome him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aristarchus my fellow prisoner greets you, and Mark the cousin of Barnabas (about whom you received instructions—if he comes to you, welcome him),

verses.rationale: Keeps the second name, circumcision identity and restricted group claim.
verses.before: Jesus who is called Justus also greets you. These are the only ones from the circumcision who are my fellow workers for God’s kingdom, and they have been a comfort to me.
verses.after: Jesus who is called Justus also greets you. These are the only circumcised coworkers for God's kingdom, and they have been a comfort to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Jesus who is called Justus. These are the only ones of the circumcision among my fellow workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.

verses.rationale: Preserves belonging, slave status, prayer struggle and both desired qualities.
verses.before: Epaphras, who is one of you, a slave of Christ Jesus, greets you. He is always struggling for you in his prayers so that you may stand mature and fully assured in everything God wills.
verses.after: Epaphras, who is one of you, a slave of Christ Jesus, greets you. He is always struggling for you in his prayers, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in all God's will.
verses.tsw_comparator: Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ Jesus, greets you, always striving on your behalf in his prayers, that you may stand mature and fully assured in all the will of God.

verses.rationale: Retains testimony, costly labor and both named neighboring communities.
verses.before: For I testify about him that he works hard for you and for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis.
verses.after: For I testify that he works hard for you and for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I bear him witness that he has labored much for you and for those in Laodicea and in Hierapolis.

verses.rationale: Keeps both names and Luke's stated occupation.
verses.before: Luke, the beloved physician, greets you, and so does Demas.
verses.after: Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas greet you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Luke the beloved physician greets you, as does Demas.

verses.rationale: Preserves the pinned feminine name and pronoun without harmonizing another tradition.
verses.before: Greet the brothers and sisters in Laodicea, and Nympha and the church in her house.
verses.after: Greet the brothers and sisters in Laodicea, as well as Nympha and the church in her house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet the brothers and sisters in Laodicea, and Nympha and the church in her house.

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal public reading and both letters without identifying the other letter.
verses.before: When this letter has been read among you, make sure it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and you in turn should read the letter from Laodicea.
verses.after: After this letter has been read among you, have it read in the church of the Laodiceans too; and you in turn should read the letter from Laodicea.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when this letter has been read among you, have it also read in the church of the Laodiceans; and you, in turn, read the letter from Laodicea.

verses.rationale: Retains direct address, received service and completion command.
verses.before: Tell Archippus, “Pay attention to the ministry you received in the Lord, so that you fulfill it.”
verses.after: Tell Archippus, “Pay attention to the ministry you received in the Lord, so that you fulfill it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And say to Archippus, “See that you fulfill the ministry that you received in the Lord.”

verses.rationale: Preserves autograph claim, imprisonment reminder and short plural blessing.
verses.before: I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.
verses.after: I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.
